references.text: Verse 9 sets the scene for the blessing given in verse 18; together they form a continuous account of the transfer of the birthright.
A theological contrast between Esau, who deceitfully asks for the birthright (27:19), and Joseph, who asks his father to recognize the younger son as the firstborn according to God's will (48:18).
A thematic parallel showing God's sovereignty in choosing the younger over the older: Esau sold his right (25:31), while Joseph asks his father to give the birthright to the younger son (48:18).
A contrasting parallel: In 27:32, 'firstborn' is used as a lie to steal a blessing, whereas in 48:18 it is correctly used by Joseph to ask that God's plan (the younger over the older) be fulfilled.
A thematic link emphasizing that the birthright is transferable: Esau sold his (25:33), while Joseph asks his father to give it to the younger son (48:18).
A direct narrative connection: 49:26 summarizes and confirms the blessing given through the laying on of hands in 48:18.
